spells.name: Find Steed
spells.description:
You summon a spirit that assumes the form of an unusually intelligent, strong, and loyal steed, creating a long-lasting bond with it. Appearing in an unoccupied space within range, the steed takes on a form that you choose: a warhorse, a pony, a camel, an elk, or a mastiff. (Your GM might allow other animals to be summoned as steeds.) The steed has the statistics of the chosen form, though it is a celestial, fey, or fiend (your choice) instead of its normal type. Additionally, if your steed has an Intelligence of 5 or less, its Intelligence becomes 6, and it gains the ability to understand one language of your choice that you speak.

Your steed serves you as a mount, both in combat and out, and you have an instinctive bond with it that allows you to fight as a seamless unit. While mounted on your steed, you can make any spell you cast that targets only you also target your steed.

When the steed drops to 0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form. You can also dismiss your steed at any time as an action, causing it to disappear. In either case, casting this spell again summons the same steed, restored to its hit point maximum.

While your steed is within 1 mile of you, you can communicate with each other telepathically.

You can't have more than one steed bonded by this spell at a time. As an action, you can release the steed from its bond at any time, causing it to disappear.

spells.name: Lesser Restoration
spells.description: End one disease or condition: blinded, deafened, paralyzed, or poisoned.

spells.name: Zone of Truth
spells.description:
You create a magical zone that guards against deception in a 15-foot-radius sphere centered on a point of your choice within range. Until the spell ends, a creature that enters the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, a creature can’t speak a deliberate lie while in the radius. You know whether each creature succeeds or fails on its saving throw.

An affected creature is aware of the spell and can thus avoid answering questions to which it would normally respond with a lie. Such creatures can be evasive in its answers as long as it remains within the boundaries of the truth.

monsterData.ac_desc: Alabaster Plating, Coin-Scale Platters, Heavy Aegis
monsterData.languages: Sura-Khai, Common (speaks with an arrogant, aristocratic cadence)

traits.name: Grey-Powder Bonding (from 5 lbs Grey Powder)
traits.description: The alchemical binding agent has sealed the construct's joints against wear and impact. Critical hits scored against the Centurion become normal hits. Resistant to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

traits.name: Dual-Cognition Array (from Noble Head & Loom-Guard Head)
traits.description: The noble's tactical intellect combined with the secondary optical processor grants the Centurion advantage on initiative rolls, and it cannot be surprised.

traits.name: Patrician Arrogance (from Noble Head & 20 Sura-Khai Coins)
traits.description: The Centurion is immune to the frightened condition. When it speaks commands in combat, any non-noble Ash Elf or commoner within 30 feet who can hear it has disadvantage on saving throws against being frightened.

traits.name: Thermodynamic Boiler (from Ruby, Sapphire, & 5 lbs Diluted Spark)
traits.description: The internal chamber constantly boils the liquid Azure Spark using thermal ruby heat. The Centurion's melee attacks deal an extra 1d6 lightning or fire damage (included below).

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The Centurion makes two attacks: one with its Coin-Plated Shield Bash and one with its Fanged Weaver-Scourge.

actions.name: Fanged Weaver-Scourge
actions.description: Melee weapon attack: +7 to hit, reach 15ft, one target. Hit: 8 (1d8+4) slashing damage plus 7 (2d6) poison damage. Target must succeed on DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned until end of its next turn. While poisoned this way, creature's movement speed is reduced to 0 as spider venom numbs its nerves.

actions.name: Coin-Plated Shield Bash
actions.description: Melee weapon attack: +7 to hit, reach 5ft, one target. Hit: 9 (1d10+4) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (1d6) fire damage. If target is Large or smaller, it must succeed on DC 15 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

actions.name: Faucet Spark-Jet
actions.description: (Recharge 5-6) The Centurion unleashes a pressurized stream of superheated, electrified cyan fluid from the gold faucet in its chest. 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in that line must make DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) lightning damage plus 14 (4d6) fire damage on failed save, or half as much on success.

reactions.name: Patrician's Aegis
reactions.description: When an attacker that the Centurion can see makes a melee attack against an ally within 5 feet of it (such as Rainlyn), the Centurion interposes its heavy coin-studded shield, imposing disadvantage on the attack roll.

monsterData.description: Large Construct (Undead Hybrid), Lawful Evil. Noble amalgam of alabaster plating, coin-scale platters, and heavy aegis. Speaks with arrogant aristocratic cadence. Constructed from noble head, loom-guard head, gold platters, Sura-Khai coins, ruby, sapphire, and diluted spark.

The Sura-Khai Data-Spike (The "Cylinder / Key")
Wondrous Item, Uncommon
A sleek, heavy cylinder of polished obsidian with a glowing cyan tip. It looks exactly like the "battery" symbol from the puzzle.
The Lore: This is an ancient master-key used by Sura-Khai architects.
The Mechanic: This item has 1 Charge. Once used, the cyan light dies, and it becomes a mundane piece of obsidian. Probably a key?


Loom-Net (Recharge 5-6). Ranged Weapon Attack: +2 to hit, range 15/30 ft., one target. Hit: The target is Restrained by a net of woven ghostly cyan light (escape DC 12). While restrained, the target takes 3 (1d6) force damage at the start of each of its turns


Sura-Khai Luxury Cache: Tucked away in a nearby basalt chest are 150 Sura-Khai Coins and a raw, uncut Amber Gemstone worth 50 GP

Amulet with misty step once per day

Perfect heavy sphere of obsidian glass (wonderous)
The Lore: This is an exceptionally rare, intact military-grade Sura-Khai power cell.
The Campaign Impact:

The Wake-Up: The pure energy within this sphere contains enough raw power to instantly awaken the Cryo-Suspended Sura-Khai Ancestor resting in their warehouse without killing him or requiring complex alchemy.

Power Source:
A dark magic looms inside. Perhaps someone may be interested in this object.


Scarf of the Vent-Walker Wondrous Item, Uncommon A thick, soot-stained wool and fungal-leather wrap worn around the mouth and nose. Properties: While wearing this scarf, you are immune to the choking effects of heavy volcanic smoke, ash storms, and poisonous spores. You have advantage on saving throws against airborne poisons and diseases (including inhaled Blight spores).


Thermal Chain-Snare (Recharge 5-6): The Vanguard hurls heated, barbed basalt-iron chains at a creature within 20 feet. The target must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure: The target takes 14 (4d6) fire damage, is pulled up to 15 feet toward the Vanguard, and is Restrained. While restrained, the target takes 7 (2d6) fire damage at the start of each of its turns. A creature can use its action to make a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check, snapping or slipping the chains on a success.


Fish Suit Source: Spelljammer: Adventures in Space - Astral Adventurer's Guide Wondrous item, Very Rare This bulky suit, which fully encases your head and body, takes 1 minute to don or doff. While worn, it enables you to breathe in an airless environment and renders you immune to the harmful effects of any gas that surrounds you. The suit also grants you a swimming speed equal to your walking speed while underwater, or a flying speed equal to your walking speed in an environment with no gravity.

feats.name: Great Weapon Master
feats.description: You've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage, letting its momentum empower your strikes. You gain the following benefits: On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action. Before you make a melee attack with a heavy weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

effects.other_mechanical: Bonus action melee attack on crit or reducing creature to 0 HP with melee weapon; -5 attack/+10 damage with proficient heavy melee weapon (optional)

feats.name: Polearm Master
feats.description: You can keep your enemies at bay with reach weapons. You gain the following benefits: When you take the Attack action and attack with only a glaive, halberd, or quarterstaff, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the opposite end of the weapon; this attack uses the same ability modifier as the primary attack. The weapon's damage die for this attack is a d4, and it deals bludgeoning damage. While you are wielding a glaive, halberd, pike, or quarterstaff, other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter the reach you have with that weapon.

effects.other_mechanical: Bonus action: d4 bludgeoning attack with butt end of glaive/halberd/quarterstaff; opportunity attack when creature enters reach with glaive/halberd/pike/quarterstaff

The chosen space must be on a surface or in a liquid that can support the target without the target having to squeeze.
spells.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the range of the spell increases by 30 feet for each slot level above 2nd.

spells.name: Snare

components.material_cost: 25 feet of rope, which the spell consumes

spells.description:
As you cast this spell, you use the rope to create a circle with a 5-foot radius on the ground or the floor. When you finish casting, the rope disappears and the circle becomes a magic trap.

This trap is nearly invisible, requiring a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC to be discerned.

The trap triggers when a Small, Medium, or Large creature moves onto the ground or the floor in the spell’s radius. That creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be magically hoisted into the air, leaving it hanging upside down 3 feet above the ground or the floor. The creature is restrained there until the spell ends.

A restrained creature can make a Dexterity saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Alternatively, the creature or someone else who can reach it can use an action to make an Intelligence (Arcana) check against your spell save DC. On a success, the restrained effect ends.

After the trap is triggered, the spell ends when no creature is restrained by it.

spells.name: Dragon's Breath

components.material_cost: a hot pepper

spells.description: You touch one willing creature and imbue it with the power to spew magical energy from its mouth, provided it has one. Choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, or poison. Until the spell ends, the creature can use an action to exhale energy of the chosen type in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 3d6 damage of the chosen type on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
spells.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 2nd.

spells.name: Scribe's Luminescence

spells.description: physically scribe or carve text onto a surface for the duration. When you finish, the script glows with a steady, heatless light that sheds bright light in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet. The effect is permanent unless physically destroyed or dispelled by magic. The light can be blocked by covering the script with an opaque object.
spells.higher_levels: additional spell effects decided by dm at higher lvls

components.material_cost: a sprinkling of holy water

spells.description: Up to 3 creatures: add 1d4 to attack rolls and saving throws. +1 creature per slot above 1st.

spells.name: Leomund's Tiny Hut

components.material_cost: (a small crystal bead)

spells.description:
A 10-foot-radius immobile dome of force springs into existence around and above you and remains stationary for the duration. The spell ends if you leave its area.

Nine creatures of Medium size or smaller can fit inside the dome with you. The spell fails if its area includes a larger creature or more than nine creatures. Creatures and objects within the dome when you cast this spell can move through it freely. All other creatures and objects are barred from passing through it. Spells and other magical effects can't extend through the dome or be cast through it. The atmosphere inside the space is comfortable and dry, regardless of the weather outside.

Until the spell ends, you can command the interior to become dimly lit or dark. The dome is opaque from the outside, of any color you choose, but it is transparent from the inside.

spells.name: Glyph of Warding

components.material_cost: (incense and powdered diamond worth at least 200 gp, which the spell consumes)

spells.description:
When you cast this spell, you inscribe a glyph that creates a magical effect triggered by other creatures, either upon a surface (such as a table or a section of floor or wall) or within an object that can be closed (such as a book, a scroll, or a treasure chest) to conceal the glyph. The glyph can cover an area no larger than 10 feet in diameter. If the surface or object is moved more than 10 feet from where you cast this spell, the glyph is broken, and the spell ends without being triggered.

The glyph is nearly invisible and requires a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC to be found.

You decide what triggers the glyph when you cast the spell. For glyphs inscribed on a surface, the most typical triggers include touching or standing on the glyph, removing another object covering the glyph, approaching within a certain distance of the glyph, or manipulating the object on which the glyph is inscribed. For glyphs inscribed within an object, the most common triggers include opening that object, approaching within a certain distance of the object, or seeing or reading the glyph. Once a glyph is triggered, this spell ends.

You can further refine the trigger so the spell activates only under certain circumstances or according to physical characteristics (such as height or weight), creature kind (for example, the ward could be set to affect aberrations or drow), or alignment. You can also set conditions for creatures that don’t trigger the glyph, such as those who say a certain password.

When you inscribe the glyph, choose explosive runes or a spell glyph.

Explosive Runes. When triggered, the glyph erupts with magical energy in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on the glyph. The sphere spreads around corners. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 5d8 acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage on a failed saving throw (your choice when you create the glyph), or half as much damage on a successful one.

Spell Glyph. You can store a prepared spell of 3rd level or lower in the glyph by casting it as part of creating the glyph. The spell must target a single creature or an area. The spell being stored has no immediate effect when cast in this way. When the glyph is triggered, the stored spell is cast. If the spell has a target, it targets the creature that triggered the glyph. If the spell affects an area, the area is centered on that creature. If the spell summons hostile creatures or creates harmful objects or traps, they appear as close as possible to the intruder and attack it. If the spell requires concentration, it lasts until the end of its full duration.
spells.higher_levels: At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage of an explosive runes glyph increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd. If you create a spell glyph, you can store any spell of up to the same level as the slot you use for the glyph of warding.

spells.name: Slow

components.material_cost: a drop of molasses

spells.description:
You alter time around up to six creatures of your choice in a 40-foot cube within range. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be affected by this spell for the duration.

An affected target’s speed is halved, it takes a -2 penalty to AC and Dexterity saving throws, and it can’t use reactions. On its turn, it can use either an action or a bonus action, not both. Regardless of the creature’s abilities or magic items, it can’t make more than one melee or ranged attack during its turn.

If the creature attempts to cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action, roll a d20. On an 11 or higher, the spell doesn’t take effect until the creature’s next turn, and the creature must use its action on that turn to complete the spell. If it can’t, the spell is wasted.

A creature affected by this spell makes another Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save, the effect ends for it.

spells.name: Fireball

components.material_cost: a tiny ball of bat guano and sulfur

spells.description: 20ft radius sphere: DEX save or 8d6 fire (half on save). Ignites flammable objects. +1d6 per slot above 3rd.

spells.name: Raelyn's Aegis Shell
spells.duration: 1 reaction, taken when you or a creature within 30 feet is targeted by an attack or forced to make a Dexterity saving throw.
spells.description: You instantly project a 10-foot-radius dome of protective energy centered on a point you can see within range. Your concentration on any other spell immediately ends. The dome has 30 hit points. No weapon attacks, spell attacks, or area-of-effect spells can pass through the perimeter of the dome from the outside or the inside. Any damage that would pass through the dome is applied to the dome's hit points instead. If an effect deals more damage than the dome has hit points remaining, the dome shatters, and any remaining damage carries over to the targets inside. Spells cast from outside the dome cannot originate inside it. If a creature attempts to teleport into or out of the dome, it must first succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC, or the teleportation fails and the action is wasted.
spells.higher_levels: when cast using a spell of 4th lvl or higher add 10hp per spell level above 3rd

spells.name: Counterspell
spells.description: When creature casts spell of 3rd level or lower: it fails. For 4th+: ability check vs DC 10 + spell level. Auto-counter with higher slot.

spells.name: Fabricate
spells.description:
You convert raw materials into products of the same material. For example, you can fabricate a wooden bridge from a clump of trees, a rope from a patch of hemp, and clothes from flax or wool.

Choose raw materials that you can see within range. You can fabricate a Large or smaller object (contained within a 10-foot cube, or eight connected 5-foot cubes), given a sufficient quantity of raw material. If you are working with metal, stone, or another mineral substance, however, the fabricated object can be no larger than Medium (contained within a single 5-foot cube). The quality of objects made by the spell is commensurate with the quality of the raw materials.

Creatures or magic items can’t be created or transmuted by this spell. You also can’t use it to create items that ordinarily require a high degree of craftsmanship, such as jewelry, weapons, glass, or armor, unless you have proficiency with the type of artisan’s tools used to craft such objects

spells.name: Sickening Radiance
spells.description:
Dim, greenish light spreads within a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range. The light spreads around corners, and it lasts until the spell ends.

When a creature moves into the spell’s area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, that creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 4d10 radiant damage, and it suffers one level of exhaustion and emits a dim, greenish light in a 5-foot radius. This light makes it impossible for the creature to benefit from being invisible. The light and any levels of exhaustion caused by this spell go away when the spell ends.

spells.name: Spirit Of Death

components.material_cost: (a gilded playing card worth at least 400 gp and depicting an avatar of death)

spells.description:
You call forth a spirit that embodies death. The spirit manifests in an unoccupied space you can see within range and uses the reaper spirit stat block. The spirit disappears when it is reduced to 0 hit points or when the spell ends.

The spirit is an ally to you and your companions. In combat, the spirit shares your initiative count and takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don’t issue the spirit any commands, it takes the Dodge action and uses its movement to avoid danger.
spells.higher_levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, use the higher level wherever the spell’s level appears in the reaper spirit stat block.

spells.name: Leomund's Secret Chest

components.material_cost: (an exquisite chest, 3 feet by 2 feet by 2 feet, constructed from rare materials worth at least 5,000 gp, and a Tiny replica made from the same materials worth at least 50 gp)

spells.description:
You hide a chest, and all its contents, on the Ethereal Plane. You must touch the chest and the miniature replica that serves as a material component for the spell. The chest can contain up to 12 cubic feet of nonliving material (3 feet by 2 feet by 2 feet).

While the chest remains on the Ethereal Plane, you can use an action and touch the replica to recall the chest. It appears in an unoccupied space on the ground within 5 feet of you. You can send the chest back to the Ethereal Plane by using an action and touching both the chest and the replica.

After 60 days, there is a cumulative 5 percent chance per day that the spell’s effect ends. This effect ends if you cast this spell again, if the smaller replica chest is destroyed, or if you choose to end the spell as an action. If the spell ends and the larger chest is on the Ethereal Plane, it is irretrievably lost

spells.name: Sleep

components.material_cost: a pinch of fine sand rose petals or a cricket

spells.description: 5d8 HP pool: creatures in 20ft sphere become unconscious in ascending HP order until pool exhausted. +2d8 per slot above 1st.

spells.name: Control Water

components.material_cost: (a drop of water and a pinch of dust)

spells.description:
Until the spell ends, you control any freestanding water inside an area you choose that is a cube up to 100 feet on a side. You can choose from any of the following effects when you cast this spell. As an action on your turn, you can repeat the same effect or choose a different one.

Flood. You cause the water level of all standing water in the area to rise by as much as 20 feet. If the area includes a shore, the flooding water spills over onto dry land. If you choose an area in a large body of water, you instead create a 20-foot tall wave that travels from one side of the area to the other and then crashes down. Any Huge or smaller vehicles in the wave’s path are carried with it to the other side. Any Huge or smaller vehicles struck by the wave have a 25 percent chance of capsizing. The water level remains elevated until the spell ends or you choose a different effect. If this effect produced a wave, the wave repeats on the start of your next turn while the flood effect lasts.

Part Water. You cause water in the area to move apart and create a trench. The trench extends across the spell’s area, and the separated water forms a wall to either side. The trench remains until the spell ends or you choose a different effect. The water then slowly fills in the trench over the course of the next round until the normal water level is restored.

Redirect Flow. You cause flowing water in the area to move in a direction you choose, even if the water has to flow over obstacles, up walls, or in other unlikely directions. The water in the area moves as you direct it, but once it moves beyond the spell’s area, it resumes its flow based on the terrain conditions. The water continues to move in the direction you chose until the spell ends or you choose a different effect.

Whirlpool. This effect requires a body of water at least 50 feet square and 25 feet deep. You cause a whirlpool to form in the center of the area. The whirlpool forms a vortex that is 5 feet wide at the base, up to 50 feet wide at the top, and 25 feet tall. Any creature or object in the water and within 25 feet of the vortex is pulled 10 feet toward it. A creature can swim away from the vortex by making a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC.

When a creature enters the vortex for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage and is caught in the vortex until the spell ends. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage, and isn’t caught in the vortex. A creature caught in the vortex can use its action to try to swim away from the vortex as described above, but has disadvantage on the Strength (Athletics) check to do so.

The first time each turn that an object enters the vortex, the object takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage, this damage occurs each round it remains in the vortex.

feats.name: Fey Touched
feats.description: Your exposure to the Feywild's magic has changed you, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn the misty step spell and one 1st-level spell of your choice from the divination or enchantment school of magic. You can cast each of these spells without expending a spell slot once per long rest. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for them (choose when you select this feat).

effects.other_mechanical: Learn Misty Step + 1 divination/enchantment 1st-level spell; cast each 1/long rest without spell slot; INT/WIS/CHA spellcasting

feats.name: Telekinetic
feats.description: You learn to move things with your mind, granting you the following benefits: Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20. You learn the mage hand cantrip. You can cast it without verbal or somatic components, and you can make the spectral hand invisible. If you already know this cantrip, you can use it as a bonus action and its range increases by 30 feet. As a bonus action, you can try to telekinetically shove a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + the ability modifier of the score increased by this feat) or be moved 5 feet toward or away from you. A creature can choose to fail this save.

effects.other_mechanical: Mage Hand (no V/S, invisible hand); if already known: bonus action + 30ft range; bonus action: telekinetic shove 5ft, STR save DC 8+prof+ability mod; can choose to fail

monsterData.name: EVELYN (SUMMONED FORM)
resistances: Cold, Necrotic; Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from Nonmagical Attacks
monsterData.languages: Telepathy 60 ft. (Summoner only), understands Sura-Khai and Common but rarely speaks aloud to others

traits.name: Phase Slip
traits.description: Evelyn can move through other creatures and solid objects as if they were difficult terrain. If she ends her turn inside an object, she takes 5 (1d10) force damage.

traits.name: The Weaver's Shadow
traits.description: Evelyn is completely invisible to all creatures other than summoner while she is in heavy fog, dim light, or darkness.

traits.name: Jealous Guardian
traits.description: While Evelyn is within 5 feet of the summoning player, any melee attacks targeting summoner are made with disadvantage as her shadowy limbs lash out to deflect the blows.

actions.name: Shadow-Stitch
actions.description: Ranged Spell Attack: +[Summoners Spell Attack Modifier] to hit, range 60 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + Summoners Proficiency Bonus) necrotic damage. If the target is currently affected by Evelyn's Hex, this attack deals an additional 1d6 necrotic damage.

actions.name: Hex
actions.description: (1/Summon). As a bonus action, Evelyn can cast the Hex spell at 1st level (no spell slot required). She maintains concentration on the spell herself (Concentration save +1). She can use her bonus action on subsequent turns to transfer the Hex to a new target.

legendary_actions.name: Unmake
legendary_actions.description: (1/Day): Break the creatures weave: [1 Target] the target must make a DC 18 CON save, on failure the target rolls (1d100) and if it surpasses the creatures total HP it dies instantly. On a successful save the target instead will take (1d100) damage.

legendary_actions.name: Darkness
legendary_actions.description: (3/DAY): EVELYN shrouds her summoner in in complete darkness. The summoners body becomes blurred, shifting and wavering to all who can see them. For the duration [1 MINUTE], any creature has disadvantage on attack rolls against them. An attacker is immune to this effect if it doesn't rely on sight, as with blindsight, or can see through illusions, as with truesight.

legendary_actions.name: Foresight
legendary_actions.description: (1/Day): You touch a willing creature and bestow a limited ability to see into the immediate future. For the duration, the target has Advantage on D20 Tests, and other creatures have Disadvantage on attack rolls against it. The spell ends early if you cast it again.

reactions.name: The Petty Assistant: (Automatic)
reactions.description: If the summoner commands her to help a party member she will refuse. If the summoner attempts to aid a party member by casting any beneficial buff (this includes healing) the summoner must roll (1d20) and roll over a 15 base roll with no advantages or modifiers.

reactions.name: Sabotage: (Automatic)
reactions.description: When a creature or enemy targets a player other than the summoner Evelyn buffs the attackers damage dice by adding (1d4) to the final damage.

monsterData.description:
Doll Form (Passive Rules)
Tethered Soul: Evelyn cannot be separated from her owner. If left behind, thrown, or stolen, she vanishes in a whisper of grey smoke and reappears in the owners pocket or pack at the start of their next turn.
The Phase Barrier: No creature other than the owner can physically touch the doll. If anyone else attempts to grab her, their hands pass through her body like cold fog.
Mortal Ward: If owner takes damage that would reduce them to 0 hit points, they can use their reaction to instantly drop to 1 hit point instead. Evelyn absorbs the blow; she takes the remaining damage, her physical doll form cracks slightly, and she cannot be summoned again until owner completes a Long Rest.
The Spool of Charges: The doll has 2 charges. Owner can expend 1 charge to cast Hex through the doll (no spell slot or concentration required from owner—Evelyn handles the spell). She regains all expended charges at dawn.

monsterData.name: Mage Hand
monsterData.description:
A spectral, floating hand appears at a point you choose within range. The hand lasts for the duration or until you dismiss it as an action. The hand vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from you or if you cast this spell again.

You can use your action to control the hand. You can use the hand to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial. You can move the hand up to 30 feet each time you use it.

The hand can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

actions.name: Bonus Actions

While the target is haunted, you and the spirit sense the direction and distance to the target if it is on the same plane of existence as you. Additionally, if the target starts its turn within 10 feet of the spirit, the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the frightened condition until the start of the target’s next turn. The target remains haunted until it dies, the spirit disappears, or the spirit uses this action again.

monsterData.ac_desc: Bone Plating, Petrified Stipe & Mimic Hide
monsterData.languages: Understands Sura-Khai and Common (bound to summoner's commands)

traits.name: Adhesive Hide (from Mimic Skin)
traits.description: The colossus's outer flesh is rubbery and adhesive. When a creature hits the colossus with a melee weapon attack, the attacker must succeed on a DC 16 Strength saving throw or the weapon becomes stuck to the colossus's shifting hide. A creature can use an action to make a DC 16 Strength check to pull a stuck weapon free.

traits.name: Garnet Hearth (from 1x Garnet)
traits.description: A smoldering volcanic garnet serves as the colossus's engine. Its melee strikes and ground stomps deal additional fire damage (included in attacks). Grants resistance to cold and fire.

traits.name: Woven Resistance (from Operator Robes)
traits.description: The tattered Sura-Khai robes woven into its frame grant the colossus advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Dual-Life Frenzy: Undead Fortitude
traits.description: From 8 Dead & 8 Live Chickens. If damage reduces the colossus to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, it drops to 1 hit point instead.

traits.name: Dual-Life Frenzy: Death Thrash
traits.description: When the colossus is finally destroyed, the eight restless spirits violently burst from its chest. Each creature within 10 feet must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 14 (4d6) necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

traits.name: Siege Monster

actions.name: Multiattack

actions.name: Bladed Staff Arm

actions.name: Fanged Bone Slam

actions.name: Charnel Loom-Quake
actions.description: (Recharge 5-6) The colossus stomps its bone-encrusted foot, discharging kinetic force and necrotic shrapnel in a 20-foot radius. Each creature on the ground in that area must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. On failure: 22 (4d10) force damage plus 14 (4d6) necrotic damage and knocked prone. On success: half damage and not knocked prone.

monsterData.description: Huge Undead (Construct), Neutral Evil. A towering horrific fusion of ancient engineering and dark necromancy. Petrified giant mushroom wood bound by pale shifting mimic hide and interlocking ribcages. A rusted Sura-Khai helmet crowns its splintered skull, tattered operator robes hang like burial shrouds. In the center of its bone-plated chest burns a single glowing red garnet, pulsing with the erratic heartbeat of sixteen sacrificed lives.

  • 1 (Arcane Static): The threads overload his senses. Box is Blinded until the start of his next turn.
  • 2–4 (Dormant): The weave is quiet. Box perceives the world normally.
  • 5–6 (Thread Clarity): The glowing cyan threads snap into focus. Box gains Truesight out to 30 feet, can see the exact location of invisible creatures and magical auras, and attack rolls against him have disadvantage until the start of his next turn as he anticipates incoming strikes.

data.name: Cassian Inkwell
data.traits: Endlessly curious; writes everything down mid-conversation. Speaks in warm, theatrical flourishes but asks piercingly practical questions. Believes every stranger is a story not yet transcribed. Deflects fear with footnotes.
data.ideals: Every story deserves a truthful teller. Knowledge unrecorded is knowledge that dies twice. Small folk matter more than grand prophecies.
data.bonds: His late master, Archivist Pellon, whose last letter named this company in a cipher no scholar has cracked. The unfinished chronicle of his own life — he refuses to die with pages missing.
data.flaws: Compulsively takes notes at the worst possible moments (mid-sneak, mid-ambush). Overexplains. Cannot leave a riddle, a locked box, or an unanswered question alone. Physically frail and knows it.
data.backstory: Cassian Inkwell, 34, scribe-turned-bard of the College of Lore. Ten years copying manuscripts in the Vault of Deneir taught him two things: every legend has a seam of truth, and his master Pellon died chasing this party's name through a cipher. He left the archive with a lute he cannot fully play, a satchel of ink, and one question: why did Pellon write YOUR names in a dead tongue? He has joined the company to find out — and to chronicle whatever happens, honestly, flaws and all.

notesPages.1: Entry the First — I have joined a company of adventurers in the field. My commission is threefold: chronicle their deeds honestly, keep the party's names out of unmarked graves, and discover why Archivist Pellon wrote them in cipher before he died. First impressions pending. The table is dark, which feels dramatically appropriate. — C.I.
